purpose: Convert the already-closed retention engineering contract into concrete launch policy choices without inferring Product, Privacy, or Legal approval.

engineeringBoundary.note: Current launch policy is one operational-retention stage: 90 days. Moderation/security/legal exceptions use D4 retention holds instead of a separate 365-day tier.

decisions.productMeaning: Account/public access and owned public/private works are removed together immediately at account deletion; owned user-authored payload is physically purged by the scheduled content-retention stage within 7 days unless an active permitted hold blocks purge.

Operational detail is scrubbed at 90 days. If moderation, security, or legal necessity still exists, the D4 hold prevents the job from being claimed; once the hold no longer applies, overdue scrub becomes eligible without a separate fixed 365-day tier.

Deletion is irreversible for the user: account access, Creator presence, and owned published/private works are removed together immediately; backend payload is then physically purged within 7 days. Wand does not promise a recovery or undo window.

Only moderation, security, or legal holds are permitted. Hold create/release requires recent-auth admin authority, a recorded reason, and audit history. A hold may extend retention beyond 90 days only while the documented necessity remains; expiry should be set when a determinate end exists, otherwise explicit admin release is required.

After payload purge and operational scrub, retain only stable IDs, revision numbering/relationships, deletion-event identity, and non-sensitive structure needed to preserve integrity of historical publication/moderation/report relationships. Do not retain deleted user-authored payload or unnecessary re-identifying detail.

Database and Storage recovery copies remain separate. Recovery is restored into a non-production target first. Before any restored Community data becomes user-visible, a minimal deletion ledger outside the primary rollback domain is replayed so accounts/content deleted after the backup point cannot reappear.
decisions.providerPlanBinding: Bind the actual Supabase production backup window and external Storage-backup provider before launch. Any longer recovery-copy retention must be reviewed and disclosed.
decisions.launchComplexityChoice: No PITR requirement at launch. Prefer provider-managed daily DB backup plus one independent private Storage recovery copy path. Provider/plan selection remains production operations.

decisions.productMeaning: Wand's database timers do not control processor copies/logs. Record the actual launch provider plan/configuration, minimize data sent to processors, and disclose provider-controlled retention where material.

Launch privacy/account-deletion copy must explain, in plain language by data category, immediate account/work removal, 7-day payload purge, 90-day operational scrub, permitted moderation/security/legal holds, minimized structural records, backup copies, and provider-controlled copies/logs.

resend.note: Provider facts describe Resend's stated service retention and are not a Wand legal sufficiency conclusion.

nextAction: Obtain explicit Product/Privacy/Legal approvals or requested changes. D6 design is now concrete but production provider selection and restore drills remain pending.
